object_description: angular two-wing school complex with differentiated heights and depths
design_condition: The angular complex occupies the northwest corner between residential development, sports fields, and slopes, using the topography to form a public forecourt, an intimate courtyard yard, and varied viewing axes with the neighbouring retirement home.

positive.statement: The precise setting creates a beautiful courtyard formation toward the linden hill.

position.target: courtyard formation toward the linden hill
position.rationale: Central open space is identifiable in plan, with the courtyard edge positioned toward the stated hill.

positive.statement: The large forecourt acquires public qualities through its connection to the village and functions as a meeting point.

position.rationale: A broad exterior area lies along the lower-left building edge, representing the public forecourt.

positive.statement: The covered external staircase cleverly connects the access level with the courtyard-side break area.

position.rationale: The stair is approximated along the courtyard-side access edge between lower and raised levels.

positive.statement: The building’s differentiated heights and depths respond carefully to the surrounding buildings and topography.

position.rationale: Stepped massing and varying wing depths are clearly visible across the plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The precise, calm project is carefully edited and makes a valuable contribution in many respects.

position.rationale: The statement evaluates the project’s overall architectural contribution without identifying one spatial location.

positive.statement: The regular structural grid clearly characterizes both the facade and the internal construction.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal and vertical point patterns visibly characterize the elevations and imply the structural rhythm.

negative.statement: The cooking-unit spaces and their connection to the main staircase are too small.

position.rationale: Interior kitchen and stair relationships are not separable, so they are approximated within the lower central building zone.

negative.statement: The internal trapped caretaker rooms do not meet the requirement.

position.rationale: Internal rooms are absent from the exterior sample and placed as a constrained guess within the east wing.

negative.statement: External use of the separated area is not possible because of the lack of direct access to toilet facilities.

position.rationale: The separated external zone is approximated beside the lower east-side edge where direct service access would occur.

negative.statement: The proportions and spatial qualities of the two-storey auditorium are questionable, especially with the one-storey lunch table extension.

position.target: two-storey auditorium and lunch table extension
position.rationale: The auditorium and adjoining extension are approximated within the deeper central-right massing.

negative.statement: The skylight strips and glazed sections should ensure good internal lighting but will be difficult to darken when necessary.

position.rationale: Roof and upper façade bands suggest a constrained location for the daylight elements, though individual strips are indistinct.

negative.statement: The access corridor provides hardly any work niches suitable for groups.

position.rationale: The internal corridor is not directly visible and is approximated along the courtyard-facing circulation zone.

negative.statement: The narrow-sided primary lighting and poorly rhythmic access corridor only partially implement the pedagogical concept.

position.target: narrow-sided primary lighting and access corridor
position.rationale: The constrained placement follows the narrow west-side wing and its adjacent circulation band.
